 Your Vote Matters — And That’s Why the Experts Continue Working Together to Check Election Results
 Secretary Thomas takes action to make sure ballots were counted accurately when voters in five towns selected the same candidate more than once
 (Hartford, Connecticut) — Election Night may be over, but data gurus at the University of Connecticut’s Center for Voting Technology Research (VoTeR) keep working behind the scenes to find potential problems. And if they do, there’s a system in place to figure out what happened and get to the bottom of it.
 Those UConn experts ran the numbers and found a programming error limited to five towns. Connecticut law allows a candidate to appear on more than one party line, and the issue only affected ballots in those towns when voters selected the same candidate on multiple lines. 
 Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas ordered those towns to review all ballots by hand – known as a “recanvass” – to ensure the final totals submitted to her Office are correct.
 “I'm grateful we have so many dedicated people looking out for Connecticut voters, even after Election Day is long past,” said Secretary Thomas . “Our system is designed to get to the root of any issue that might come up, and when one does, we do something about it.”
 Following the discovery of the programming error, UConn, state election officials, and the equipment vendor reviewed results from all 169 municipalities and found that no additional towns were affected. The vendor acknowledged responsibility, and the Office is working with them to address the issue and prevent similar errors in future elections.
